receipt: Full Replogle K562 essential screen as pseudobulk differential expression: RapidGLM 1.4.1 bulk-de and edger-ql against DESeq2 and edgeR QL, every perturbation of the screen

build.configure: cmake -S clone -B clone/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBLA_VENDOR=OpenBLAS plus the paths of the extracted OpenBLAS 0.3.20 and LAPACKE (validation/local-data/numerical-deps); default project options

host: One workstation: Intel Core i9-13900KF, 125 GiB RAM; BIOS 1836, microcode 0x133, 253 W sustained and short-term limits; 4 x 32 GiB at 4,200 MT/s. Turbo is on. Two faulty performance cores (logical CPUs 8-11) are capped at 2.2 GHz and never used for timing. Every timed command is pinned to the 16 identical efficiency cores (CPUs 16-31, stock 800 MHz-4.3 GHz), one thread per core, under the shared lock after a quiet-host check. Same host setting as the 1.4.0 receipts; absolute seconds from other host settings are not directly comparable. On the user's order, every performance core (CPUs 0-15) was capped at 2.2 GHz from 2026-10-23 13:57 UTC (cap-faulty-cores.service; before that only CPUs 8-11); turbo and CPUs 16-31 were unchanged, the guarded policy kept matching, and no timed command ran on CPUs 0-15 (they held only drivers and untimed work).

version_relation.measured_release: 1.4.1 (v1.4.1, 64a8610); the paper keeps the 1.4.0 receipts (v1.4.0-dev.4, f0ecfbd) for the shared benchmarks
version_relation.code_difference: Between f0ecfbd and 64a8610 the library differs only by an early return for zero-column weighted cross-products (include/rapidglm/model.hpp) and version strings.
same_outputs_evidence: Replogle pilot (20 perturbations): every RapidGLM bulk-de and edger-ql table byte-identical to the 1.4.0 pilot (pilot-v1.4.0-final), run records equal apart from version, paths and timings; DESeq2 and edgeR outputs identical too (REPLOGLE_PSEUDOBULK_FULL.json, pilot_check).
Geuvadis chr22: the 580 chromosome-22 rows of the genome-wide 1.4.1 qtl run byte-identical to the 1.4.0 chr22 receipt run (EQTL_GENOME_WIDE.json, chr22_check).

protocol.quiet_start: Two consecutive ten-second samples with one-minute load <= 4 and every selected CPU < 20% busy (scripts/quiet_run.py); the retained samples are in timing-audit.jsonl.
protocol.cpu_policy: intel_pstate/no_turbo = 0; CPUs 16-31 scaling_min_freq 800000 and scaling_max_freq 4300000; CPUs 8-11 scaling_max_freq 2200000. Checked once per second during every supervised block and synchronously at every quiet start, with the unchanged 1.4.0 guard code (validation/receipts/v1.4.0/cpu_policy.py, policy_hook); never changed.
protocol.untimed: Preparation, comparisons, downloads and drivers on CPUs 0-7 and 12-15 under nice; CPUs 8-11 never used.
protocol.contention: others_cpu: busy time of the timed CPUs not spent by the measured commands, as a share of those CPUs over the wall time; a run above 0.05 counts as contended and is re-run.

data.source: Replogle et al. 2022, figshare file 35773219 (CC BY 4.0)
data.pseudobulk: Lane sums of the pilot (scripts/prepare_replogle.py): one sample per perturbation group and lane (gem_group)
data.skip_rule: A perturbation is skipped only where the pilot code fails on it (dataset construction or a tool); none was skipped.

audit_note: The supervised block "full" ran the four screens and then the eQTL stages; its exit 143 comes from stopping the void first tensorQTL attempt (see EQTL_GENOME_WIDE.json, reruns). All five A stages (pilotcheck and the four full screens) exited 0 on their first attempt, uncontended, with every policy check matched.
model: For each perturbation, the pilot dataset (pseudobulk_dataset in scripts/replogle_pilot.py): its samples and the 48 non-targeting samples, design ~ lane + perturbed (intercept, lane indicators for the lanes present, perturbed indicator); the perturbed coefficient is tested.

tools.rapidglm: build-1.4.1/rapidglm bulk-de CONFIG (responses counts.mtx, design x.tsv, last coefficient, threads 1)
tools.deseq2: Rscript scripts/reference_replogle_bulk.R (DESeq2 1.48.2, Wald test, no shrinkage; validation/local-data/R_library)
tools.edger: Rscript scripts/reference_replogle_edger.R (edgeR 4.6.2: filterByExpr, TMM, glmQLFit, glmQLFTest; validation/local-data/R_glmgampoi:R_library)
tools.driver: scripts/replogle_pilot.py full-prepare, full --tool T, full-compare (this change)
tools.reference_tools_used_as: black boxes through their public R interfaces

layout: One tool at a time over the whole screen; 16 single-thread workers, worker k pinned to CPU 16+k, each taking the next perturbation (sorted by name) from a shared queue; the driver on CPUs 0-7. Per perturbation: wall, CPU, peak RSS, tool-internal seconds (DESeq() fit, edgeR QL workflow) and the other processes' share of its CPU (job_others_cpu).

pilot_check.rule: Tables byte-identical; JSON run records equal after dropping version, paths, timings and fingerprints of configuration files (which hold paths).
pilot_check.note: Pilot: each job alone on CPU 16 (1.4.0 receipts run). Here: 16 single-thread jobs at once on CPUs 16-31.

agreement_notes: p-values rank identically in the discordant perturbations inspected (Spearman 1.0 over tested genes); the discoveries differ through the independent-filtering quantile each tool chose (filtering).

The largest log10 p differences are deep in the tail (p < 1e-60) at mitochondrial genes with nearly equal fold changes, e.g. RPL24, MT-ATP6: LFC -1.110 vs -1.111, p 9e-177 (RapidGLM) vs 3e-117 (DESeq2).
Without the reference implementation the reason for a policy difference cannot be checked; both tools were run as black boxes.

compression.rule: gzip -6 of every .tsv and .mtx over 64 KiB in the dataset folders
